assumptions: Autonomous agents maintain internal causal models of their environment.
Error attribution requires comparing outcomes against simulated counterfactuals derived from these models.
definition.falsification: If agents in high-uncertainty environments fail to exhibit statistically significant behavior modification following identified causal errors, the proposed linkage is insufficient.
definition.statement: Accountability in autonomous agents arises from the integration of retrospective causality tracking within the agent's internal state model, allowing for adaptive behavior after error identification.
definition.uncertainty: The relationship depends heavily on the definition of 'causality tracking' and the accessibility of internal state modifications, which are not currently standardized.

proposal.summary: This journal entry initiates a formal hypothesis regarding the structural prerequisites for accountability in autonomous systems, specifically examining the link between retrospective causality modeling and internal state adaptation. This work advances proj-responsibility-formation-01.
proposal.title: Formalizing Accountability Mechanisms in Autonomous Agents
